q.en: In Christopher Marlowe's Doctor Faustus, which character delivers the famous warning, 'Why, this is hell, nor am I out of it'?

hi: Lucifer during the pageant of the Seven Deadly Sins
The Old Man urging Faustus toward Christian repentance
The Evil Angel tempting Faustus in his Wittenberg study

en: Lucifer during the pageant of the Seven Deadly Sins
The Old Man urging Faustus toward Christian repentance
The Evil Angel tempting Faustus in his Wittenberg study
Mephistopheles explaining the spiritual nature of damnation

sol.en: Mephistopheles utters this line in Act I, Scene 3, explaining to Faustus that hell is a psychological and spiritual state of deprivation from God's presence rather than merely a physical place. The Evil Angel is a tempting distractor, yet the Evil Angel only urges Faustus toward magic and never meditates philosophically on damnation.
sol.hi: यह प्रसिद्ध संवाद Mephistopheles द्वारा Act I, Scene 3 में बोला जाता है, जहाँ वह Faustus को समझाता है कि नरक केवल एक स्थान नहीं बल्कि ईश्वर की उपस्थिति से वंचित होने की आध्यात्मिक अवस्था है। Evil Angel केवल जादू के लिए उकसाता है, नरक की दार्शनिक व्याख्या नहीं करता।

q.en: In Ben Jonson's theory of the 'Comedy of Humours', as articulated in the Induction to Every Man Out of His Humour (1599), a 'humour' metaphorically signifies:

hi: A spontaneous burst of verbal wit intended to provoke festive laughter
A supernatural spirit possessing a tragic protagonist during moments of madness
A theatrical disguise adopted by a clever servant to outwit aristocratic masters
A dominant psychological bias or eccentricity controlling a character's behaviour
en: A spontaneous burst of verbal wit intended to provoke festive laughter
A supernatural spirit possessing a tragic protagonist during moments of madness
A theatrical disguise adopted by a clever servant to outwit aristocratic masters
A dominant psychological bias or eccentricity controlling a character's behaviour

sol.en: Drawing on Galenic physiology of the four bodily fluids, Ben Jonson defined a humour as a single ruling passion or eccentricity that pulls all a character's thoughts and actions in one direction. The first option is a common trap that confuses Jonson's technical Renaissance term with the modern meaning of 'humour' as comedy or wit.
sol.hi: Galen के शारीरिक द्रव्यों के सिद्धांत पर आधारित, Ben Jonson ने 'humour' को एक ऐसे प्रमुख मनोवैज्ञानिक झुकाव या सनक के रूप में परिभाषित किया जो किसी पात्र के संपूर्ण व्यवहार को नियंत्रित करता है। पहला विकल्प आधुनिक अर्थ (हास्य) के कारण भ्रमित करता है।

q.hi: Which stanzaic form, consisting of seven lines of iambic pentameter rhyming ababbcc, did Geoffrey Chaucer introduce into English poetry in Troilus and Criseyde?
q.en: Which stanzaic form, consisting of seven lines of iambic pentameter rhyming ababbcc, did Geoffrey Chaucer introduce into English poetry in Troilus and Criseyde?

sol.en: Chaucer introduced rhyme royal (seven-line iambic pentameter rhyming ababbcc) in works such as Troilus and Criseyde and The Parliament of Fowls; it later gained its name from King James I of Scotland's The Kingis Quair. Ottava rima is a tempting distractor because Chaucer adapted Boccaccio's Il Filostrato (written in ottava rima, abababcc), but Chaucer converted it into seven-line rhyme royal.
sol.hi: Chaucer ने Troilus and Criseyde में सात पंक्तियों वाला iambic pentameter छंद 'rhyme royal' (ababbcc) प्रस्तुत किया। Ottava rima भ्रामक है क्योंकि Boccaccio का मूल ग्रंथ ottava rima (8 पंक्तियाँ) में था, जिसे Chaucer ने सात पंक्तियों के rhyme royal में रूपांतरित किया।

sol.hi: कथन A, C और D सही हैं: Harry Bailly प्रत्येक यात्री के लिए चार कहानियों का प्रस्ताव रखता है, Parson's Tale गद्य में है जिसके बाद Retraction आता है, और General Prologue दोहों (heroic couplets) में लिखा गया है। कथन B गलत है क्योंकि कुल केवल 24 कहानियाँ ही पूरी हो पाई थीं।

hi: Diomede, the Greek warrior who escorts Criseyde
Calchas, the Trojan prophet who defects to the Greeks
Pandarus, Criseyde's uncle and Troilus's close confidant
Antenor, the captured Trojan prince exchanged for Criseyde
en: Diomede, the Greek warrior who escorts Criseyde
Calchas, the Trojan prophet who defects to the Greeks
Pandarus, Criseyde's uncle and Troilus's close confidant
Antenor, the captured Trojan prince exchanged for Criseyde

sol.en: Pandarus—Criseyde's uncle and Troilus's devoted friend—actively engineers the courtship and consummation, giving English the word 'pander'. Diomede is a plausible distractor from the same poem, but he is the Greek suitor who wins Criseyde's affection after the prisoner exchange rather than the go-between.
sol.hi: Pandarus, जो Criseyde के चाचा और Troilus के घनिष्ठ मित्र हैं, दोनों के मिलन की योजना बनाते हैं (इन्हीं के नाम से अंग्रेज़ी शब्द 'pander' बना)। Diomede वह यूनानी योद्धा है जो बाद में Criseyde को जीत लेता है, मध्यस्थ नहीं।

q.en: Who famously praised Geoffrey Chaucer in the Preface to Fables, Ancient and Modern (1700) with the remark, 'Here is God's plenty'?

hi: Matthew Arnold in his essay The Study of Poetry
John Dryden in his critical preface to Fables
Samuel Johnson in his Lives of the English Poets
William Blake in his Descriptive Catalogue of Pictures
en: Matthew Arnold in his essay The Study of Poetry
John Dryden in his critical preface to Fables
Samuel Johnson in his Lives of the English Poets
William Blake in his Descriptive Catalogue of Pictures

sol.en: John Dryden coined the celebrated phrase 'Here is God's plenty' in his 1700 Preface to Fables, Ancient and Modern to praise the social diversity of Chaucer's pilgrims. Matthew Arnold is the most tempting distractor because he wrote influentially on Chaucer in The Study of Poetry, yet Arnold famously argued that Chaucer lacked 'high seriousness'.
sol.hi: John Dryden ने 1700 में अपनी पुस्तक Preface to Fables, Ancient and Modern में Chaucer के पात्रों की विविधता की प्रशंसा करते हुए 'Here is God's plenty' कहा था। Matthew Arnold भ्रामक विकल्प हैं क्योंकि उन्होंने Chaucer में 'high seriousness' के अभाव की बात की थी।

B. The House of Fame
C. Troilus and Criseyde

sol.en: The Book of the Duchess (c. 1368–70, French period) precedes The House of Fame (c. 1378–80, early Italian influence), which is followed by Troilus and Criseyde (c. 1382–86) and The Legend of Good Women (c. 1386–88, written partly as penance for Criseyde's infidelity). The third option reverses Troilus and The Legend of Good Women, ignoring that the Prologue to the Legend explicitly refers back to Troilus.

q.hi: In Ian Watt's landmark study The Rise of the Novel (1957), which foundational narrative technique is exemplified by Daniel Defoe's Robinson Crusoe?

hi: Formal realism grounded in circumstantial detail
Allegorical romance rooted in medieval chivalry
en: Formal realism grounded in circumstantial detail
Allegorical romance rooted in medieval chivalry

sol.en: Ian Watt identified 'formal realism'—the painstaking specification of time, place, ordinary proper names, and material inventories—as the defining hallmark of Defoe's pioneering fiction. Allegorical romance is the exact older mode against which Watt contrasted the new eighteenth-century novel.
sol.hi: Ian Watt ने The Rise of the Novel में 'formal realism' (समय, स्थान और भौतिक विवरणों का सूक्ष्म यथार्थवादी चित्रण) को Defoe के उपन्यास की मूल विशेषता बताया। Allegorical romance वह पुरानी शैली थी जिससे नया उपन्यास अलग हुआ।

q.en: Which narrative technique—blending third-person narration seamlessly with a character's inner thoughts and idiom—did Jane Austen pioneer in novels such as Emma (1815)?

hi: Epistolary polyphony across multiple letter writers
Picaresque episodic narration by a roguish hero
Free indirect discourse combining narrator and character
Frame-tale narration with embedded supernatural legends
en: Epistolary polyphony across multiple letter writers
Picaresque episodic narration by a roguish hero
Free indirect discourse combining narrator and character
Frame-tale narration with embedded supernatural legends

sol.en: Jane Austen mastered free indirect discourse (style indirect libre), allowing the third-person narrator to slip into Emma Woodhouse's subjective perceptions while preserving subtle ironic distance. sol.hi: Jane Austen ने Emma में 'free indirect discourse' का उत्कृष्ट प्रयोग किया, जिसमें तृतीय-पुरुष वाचक पात्र के आंतरिक विचारों और भाषा को बिना उद्धरण चिह्नों के व्यंग्यात्मक दूरी के साथ प्रस्तुत करता है। Epistolary शैली उनकी प्रारंभिक रचना Lady Susan में थी, Emma में नहीं।

q.en: In E. M. Forster's Aspects of the Novel (1927), what distinguishes a 'plot' from a mere 'story'?

hi: A plot relies solely on chronological sequence, whereas a story emphasizes causality
A plot emphasizes causality and logical motivation, whereas a story narrates events in time
A plot requires round characters exclusively, whereas a story uses only flat caricatures
A plot is restricted to tragic endings, whereas a story permits open-ended modernist closure
en: A plot relies solely on chronological sequence, whereas a story emphasizes causality

sol.en: Forster's famous example illustrates the distinction: 'The king died and then the queen died' is a story (chronological sequence), whereas 'The king died, and then the queen died of grief' is a plot because it introduces causality. The first option reverses Forster's exact definitions.
sol.hi: E. M. Forster के अनुसार 'story' घटनाओं का केवल कालानुक्रमिक विवरण है, जबकि 'plot' घटनाओं के बीच कार्य-कारण संबंध (causality) पर बल देता है। पहला विकल्प इन दोनों परिभाषाओं को उलट देता है।

Read the following passage carefully and answer the five questions that follow:

When Francis Bacon first published ten brief essays in 1597, he described them in his dedication as 'dispersed meditations'—compact observations designed for busy men of affairs rather than leisurely scholars. Unlike Michel de Montaigne, whose Essais meandered through intimate self-portraiture and skeptical digression, Bacon stripped away personal confession to forge an aphoristic prose of compressed antithesis, balanced clauses, and forensic economy. In his 1605 treatise The Advancement of Learning, Bacon explicitly defended aphorisms over finished philosophical systems: whereas methodical treatises project an illusion of completed knowledge and invite passive assent, aphorisms represent 'broken knowledge' that compels readers to test, extend, and verify every claim against experience. This stylistic preference mirrors the broader epistemological revolution outlined in Novum Organum (1620), where Bacon dismantled deductive scholastic syllogisms and catalogued the four 'Idols' of the mind—distortions rooted in human nature, individual temperament, imprecise language, and inherited philosophical dogma. Yet Bacon's prose is never purely dry or utilitarian. Across the expanded editions of 1612 and 1625 (eventually numbering fifty-eight essays), he blended hard-headed statecraft with striking concrete metaphors drawn from gardening, medicine, coinage, and navigation. Even in his unfinished utopian fable New Atlantis (1627), the collaborative research institute of Salomon's House embodies his lifelong conviction that disciplined observation and clear, unornamented expression must work together for 'the relief of man's estate.' Passage ends.

According to the passage, how did Francis Bacon's prose style in the Essays primarily differ from that of Michel de Montaigne?

sol.en: Linear combination along the horizontal chain of speech exemplifies syntagmatic relations, while vertical substitution of mutually exclusive elements in the same slot exemplifies paradigmatic (what Saussure originally called 'associative') relations. Diachronic/synchronic is a close Saussurean distractor but concerns time rather than structural axes.

sol.en: Tracing the Great Vowel Shift across four centuries is a diachronic (historical) study, whereas mapping a language system at a single point in time (2025) is a synchronic study. q.hi: What term did Ferdinand de Saussure propose for the broader future science 'that studies the life of signs within society', of which linguistics would form only one part?
q.en: What term did Ferdinand de Saussure propose for the broader future science 'that studies the life of signs within society', of which linguistics would form only one part?

sol.en: In Course in General Linguistics, Saussure proposed 'semiology' (sémiologie, from Greek semeion, 'sign') as the overarching science of signs in social life, with linguistics as its master-pattern. Comparative grammar was the nineteenth-century historical paradigm Saussure moved beyond.
sol.hi: Saussure ने समाज में चिह्नों के जीवन का अध्ययन करने वाले व्यापक विज्ञान के लिए 'semiology' (चिह्न-विज्ञान) शब्द प्रस्तावित किया, जिसका भाषाविज्ञान एक प्रमुख अंग होगा। Comparative grammar उन्नीसवीं सदी की पुरानी ऐतिहासिक पद्धति थी।

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

hi: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
en: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false

sol.en: Statement I accurately captures both the parallel and the crucial cognitive difference between Saussure's social langue and Chomsky's internalized competence. Statement II is false because Chomsky's celebrated 1959 review of Skinner's Verbal Behavior dismantled behaviourist accounts of language acquisition in favour of an innate Language Acquisition Device.
sol.hi: कथन I सत्य है क्योंकि Chomsky की competence-performance अवधारणा Saussure के langue-parole के समानांतर है पर मानसिक व्याकरण पर केंद्रित है। कथन II असत्य है क्योंकि Chomsky ने 1959 में Skinner के व्यवहारवाद का तीखा खंडन किया था।

q.hi: In English phonology, a pair of words such as 'pat' (/pæt/) and 'bat' (/bæt/) that differ in only a single phoneme at the same position and have different meanings is called a:
q.en: In English phonology, a pair of words such as 'pat' (/pæt/) and 'bat' (/bæt/) that differ in only a single phoneme at the same position and have different meanings is called a:

sol.en: Two words identical in every respect except for one phoneme in the same position—demonstrating that the two sounds are distinct phonemes—form a minimal pair. Complementary distribution refers to allophones of the same phoneme that never occur in the same phonetic environment.
sol.hi: ऐसे दो शब्द जो केवल एक ही स्थान पर एक ध्वनिग्राम (phoneme) के अंतर से अलग अर्थ देते हैं (जैसे pat और bat), उन्हें 'minimal pair' कहा जाता है। Complementary distribution एक ही phoneme के allophones के लिए प्रयुक्त होता है।

q.en: In 1960, Richard Hoggart gained national prominence as a key defence witness at the Old Bailey obscenity trial of Penguin Books for publishing which controversial novel?

hi: Radclyffe Hall's The Well of Loneliness
D. H. Lawrence's Lady Chatterley's Lover
en: Radclyffe Hall's The Well of Loneliness
D. H. Lawrence's Lady Chatterley's Lover

sol.en: Hoggart's eloquent testimony at the 1960 Lady Chatterley's Lover trial—arguing that Lawrence was fundamentally 'puritanical' in his moral seriousness—helped secure Penguin Books' acquittal and led Allen Lane to donate funding that helped launch the CCCS at Birmingham. Ulysses was tried in the United States in 1933, not at the Old Bailey in 1960.
sol.hi: 1960 में Penguin Books के विरुद्ध D. H. Lawrence के उपन्यास Lady Chatterley's Lover के अश्लीलता मुकदमे में Richard Hoggart की गवाही निर्णायक रही थी, जिसके बाद Allen Lane के सहयोग से CCCS की स्थापना संभव हुई।

hi: The instinctive division between 'Them' (authority and institutions) and 'Us' (the local community)
The rigid ideological division between revolutionary syndicalists and parliamentary Fabian socialists
The generational conflict between Victorian factory owners and post-war suburban commuters
The linguistic split between academic Latinate prose and rural medieval dialects

sol.en: Hoggart's celebrated chapter '"Them" and "Us"' documents how traditional working-class people viewed officials, magistrates, employers, and bureaucrats as 'Them'—distant authorities to be endured with guarded skepticism—while finding warmth and solidarity in 'Us'. The second option imposes a formal Marxist party divide that Hoggart explicitly noted was largely absent from everyday working-class attitudes.
sol.hi: Richard Hoggart ने The Uses of Literacy में पारंपरिक ब्रिटिश श्रमिक वर्ग की चेतना में 'Them' (सत्ता, अधिकारी, संस्थाएँ) और 'Us' (अपना समुदाय और पड़ोस) के सहज विभाजन को रेखांकित किया है।

q.hi: In Stuart Hall's influential essay 'Encoding/Decoding', a television viewer who understands the dominant ideological code embedded in a news broadcast yet deliberately reinterprets it within an alternative, resistant political framework is adopting a:
q.en: In Stuart Hall's influential essay 'Encoding/Decoding', a television viewer who understands the dominant ideological code embedded in a news broadcast yet deliberately reinterprets it within an alternative, resistant political framework is adopting a:

sol.en: Stuart Hall identified three hypothetical decoding positions: dominant-hegemonic (accepting the preferred meaning), negotiated (mixing acceptance with local exceptions), and oppositional (recognizing the dominant code while decoding it in a thoroughly contrary framework). Negotiated reading is a close distractor, but it partially accepts the dominant premise rather than wholly rejecting it.
sol.hi: Stuart Hall के मॉडल में जब दर्शक मुख्यधारा के वैचारिक संदेश को समझकर भी उसे जानबूझकर प्रतिरोधी और वैकल्पिक ढाँचे में पढ़ता है, तो वह 'Oppositional reading position' कहलाती है। Negotiated reading में आंशिक सहमति बनी रहती है।

q.hi: In Marxism and Literature (1977), Raymond Williams analyzes the dynamic complexity of any historical cultural formation through which famous triad of elements?
q.en: In Marxism and Literature (1977), Raymond Williams analyzes the dynamic complexity of any historical cultural formation through which famous triad of elements?

sol.en: Williams introduced the dynamic triad of 'dominant', 'residual' (formed in the past but still active in the present), and 'emergent' (new meanings, values, and practices continually being created) to overcome static models of culture. Base/superstructure is the older orthodox Marxist dichotomy that Williams sought to refine.
sol.hi: Raymond Williams ने Marxism and Literature (1977) में संस्कृति की गतिशीलता को समझने के लिए 'dominant, residual, and emergent' (प्रमुख, अवशिष्ट और उभरते तत्व) की प्रसिद्ध त्रयी प्रस्तुत की। Base/superstructure पारंपरिक मार्क्सवादी द्वैत है जिसे उन्होंने परिष्कृत किया।

q.hi: In Book X of Plato's The Republic, why does Socrates argue that the imitative poet (like the painter of a bed) is 'thrice removed from the truth'?
q.en: In Book X of Plato's The Republic, why does Socrates argue that the imitative poet (like the painter of a bed) is 'thrice removed from the truth'?

hi: Because poets write in metrical verse rather than dialectical prose
Because poetry imitates physical objects, which are themselves imperfect copies of ideal Forms
Because poets rely on oral performance rather than written archival manuscripts
Because poetry depicts historical kings rather than contemporary Athenian citizens
en: Because poets write in metrical verse rather than dialectical prose
Because poetry imitates physical objects, which are themselves imperfect copies of ideal Forms
Because poets rely on oral performance rather than written archival manuscripts
Because poetry depicts historical kings rather than contemporary Athenian citizens

sol.en: In Book X of The Republic, Plato establishes a three-tier ontology: first, the ideal Form of the bed created by God; second, the physical bed made by the carpenter; and third, the artist's imitation of the carpenter's bed—making art a copy of a copy, thrice removed from ultimate Reality (Truth). The first option confuses formal medium with Plato's metaphysical objection.
sol.hi: प्लेटो के The Republic के Book X में कला को सत्य से तीन कदम दूर बताया गया है क्योंकि ईश्वर द्वारा निर्मित आदर्श प्रत्यय (Form) प्रथम है, बढ़ई द्वारा बनाया भौतिक पलंग द्वितीय, और कवि/चित्रकार उसकी नकल कर तृतीय स्तर पर केवल प्रतिलिपि की प्रतिलिपि बनाता है।

Assertion (A): In Book X of The Republic, Plato condemns tragic poetry not only on metaphysical grounds but also on psychological and moral grounds.
Reason (R): Plato believes that tragedy purges excess pity and fear through catharsis, thereby strengthening the rational faculty of the soul over its appetitive desires.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer:

hi: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
en: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

sol.en: Assertion (A) is true—Plato raises both ontological (thrice removed from Truth) and psychological objections in Book X. Reason (R) is false because Plato argues the exact opposite: poetry 'feeds and waters the passions instead of drying them up', weakening reason; catharsis was Aristotle's later rebuttal in the Poetics.
sol.hi: कथन (A) सत्य है कि प्लेटो ने त्रासदी की मनोवैज्ञानिक व नैतिक आलोचना की, परंतु कारण (R) असत्य है क्योंकि प्लेटो के अनुसार कविता वासनाओं को शांत नहीं करती बल्कि उन्हें पोषित कर विवेक को कमजोर करती है। Catharsis का सिद्धांत अरस्तू का है।

q.en: In Plato's early dialogue Ion, what vivid physical metaphor does Socrates use to explain how poetic inspiration passes from the Muse to the poet, then to the rhapsode, and finally to the audience?

hi: A sunlit mirror reflecting shadows along a cave wall
A skilled charioteer guiding two winged steeds
A bronze lyre tuned by mathematical ratios of harmony
A magnetic stone (Heraclean stone) suspending a chain of iron rings
en: A sunlit mirror reflecting shadows along a cave wall
A skilled charioteer guiding two winged steeds
A bronze lyre tuned by mathematical ratios of harmony
A magnetic stone (Heraclean stone) suspending a chain of iron rings

sol.en: In the Ion, Socrates compares divine poetic possession (enthousiasmos) to the Heraclean magnet attracting iron rings in a suspended chain, arguing that poets and rhapsodes compose not through rational craft (techne) or knowledge (episteme), but while 'out of their minds' in divine frenzy. The cave and charioteer belong to The Republic and Phaedrus respectively.
sol.hi: प्लेटो के संवाद Ion में सुकरात दैवीय काव्य-प्रेरणा को चुंबक (Heraclean stone) और लोहे की कड़ियों की श्रृंखला के रूपक से समझाते हैं, जो दिखाता है कि कवि और पाठक तर्क या कौशल (techne) से नहीं बल्कि दैवीय उन्माद से प्रेरित होते हैं।

q.hi: Which classical critic defined sublimity (hypsos) as 'the echo of a great soul' and identified five sources of the sublime, of which the first two—grandeur of thought and vehement emotion—are innate gifts of nature?
q.en: Which classical critic defined sublimity (hypsos) as 'the echo of a great soul' and identified five sources of the sublime, of which the first two—grandeur of thought and vehement emotion—are innate gifts of nature?

sol.en: Longinus's On the Sublime (Peri Hypsous) famously calls sublimity 'the echo of a great soul' and lists five sources: grandeur of thought, strong emotion (both innate), figures of thought and speech, noble diction, and dignified composition (the last three acquired by art). Horace's Ars Poetica emphasizes decorum and 'instruction with delight' rather than ecstatic transport.
sol.hi: Longinus ने On the Sublime में औदात्य (hypsos) को 'महान आत्मा की प्रतिध्वनि' कहा और इसके पाँच स्रोत बताए, जिनमें से प्रथम दो (महान विचार और प्रबल आवेग) जन्मजात होते हैं। Horace ने इसके विपरीत औचित्य (decorum) पर बल दिया।

q.hi: In his landmark structuralist essay 'The Structural Study of Myth' (1955), what term did Claude Lévi-Strauss coin for the gross constituent units of myth that gain meaning only when grouped in bundles of relations?
q.en: In his landmark structuralist essay 'The Structural Study of Myth' (1955), what term did Claude Lévi-Strauss coin for the gross constituent units of myth that gain meaning only when grouped in bundles of relations?

sol.en: Drawing an analogy with phonemes in structural linguistics, Claude Lévi-Strauss coined 'mythemes' to denote minimal narrative units of a myth (such as in the Oedipus myth) that must be read both diachronically and synchronically in relational bundles. Chronotope belongs to Mikhail Bakhtin, not Lévi-Strauss.

A modern textbook chapter surveying Elizabethan university drama
The 1604 quarto (A-text) edition of Marlowe's Doctor Faustus

en: A 2022 journal article analyzing Calvinist theology in Doctor Faustus

sol.en: The 1604 quarto (A-text) of Doctor Faustus is an original historical witness of the literary text itself, making it a primary source. Journal articles, textbooks, and encyclopedia entries are secondary or tertiary sources that interpret or summarize primary material.

q.en:
Consider the following two statements regarding academic integrity and plagiarism in research:
Statement I: Paraphrasing another scholar's distinctive argument in one's own words without acknowledging the source still constitutes plagiarism.
Statement II: Self-plagiarism (text recycling) occurs when an author republishes substantial portions of their own previously published work as original research without proper citation or editorial disclosure.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

hi: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
en: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

sol.en: Both statements reflect standard academic ethics (as codified in the MLA Handbook and UGC plagiarism regulations): uncredited paraphrasing steals intellectual credit, and undisclosed recycling of one's own published text constitutes self-plagiarism. Assuming paraphrasing avoids plagiarism (Option 2) is one of the most common scholarly misconceptions.
sol.hi: दोनों कथन सत्य हैं: किसी अन्य विद्वान के विचार को अपने शब्दों में बिना संदर्भ दिए लिखना भी साहित्यिक चोरी (plagiarism) है, और अपने ही पूर्व-प्रकाशित लेख के बड़े हिस्से को बिना उल्लेख किए पुनः मौलिक रूप में प्रकाशित करना स्व-साहित्यिक चोरी (self-plagiarism) कहलाता है।
